clue.text: Crack big, but not black, with deeper descent

indicators.note: to crack something is to break it apart, so these letters are broken up and reassembled
says the word big is to be taken without the letter for black

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to crack a large problem while avoiding darkness, digging into deeper ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not black' removes B from BIG, leaving IG; 'Crack' scrambles IG with DEEPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a line of ancestry, which is exactly what descent means in the family sense.

clue.text: Culprits thrown out, lock flat?

indicators.note: things thrown out are cast into disarray, so the letters of the word culprits are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers are evicted and their apartment is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment and 'lock' like a fastening; really a lock is hair, worn flat against the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss curl pressed flat to the brow is a hairstyle; a lock is a tress of hair, flattened in this style.

clue.text: In leaving child, love hollow stuff

indicators.note: signals that the word in departs from the word for a child

parts.note: bambino is Italian for a baby or small child, used in English
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A parent says that when abandoning a child, love proves an empty thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo canes are hollow-stemmed grass, so the material is literally hollow stuff.

clue.text: Hungry like an actor?

parts.note: Gregory Peck, the American film star
the suffix -ish means like or somewhat, as in boyish

explanation.surface: A question whether a hungry performer resembles an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Peckish is a British colloquialism for slightly hungry, wanting a snack.

clue.text: Dance cool and bursting with energy

parts.note: to fan someone is to cool them

indicators.note: something bursting is broken open, so the letters of the word and are rearranged

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

explanation.surface: A dancer described as cool and full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting' scrambles the word 'and' into DAN. 'cool' is a verb here (to fan), not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time.

clue.text: Teams go off riding in unorthodox manner

parts.note: sides are teams in a match
eggs addle when they go off or turn rotten

explanation.surface: Sports teams set off riding horses in an odd style.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding sidesaddle, both legs on one flank of the horse, is an unconventional seat today.

clue.text: Heart of course absent in Scent of a Woman

indicators.note: points at the central letter of the word for course, the one to go
says that central letter is missing

parts.note: a channel is a course along which water flows

explanation.surface: A film title, Scent of a Woman, with the heart of a course missing from it.
explanation.walkthrough: CHANNEL has seven letters; its middle one, N, is 'absent'. 'Scent of a Woman' looks like the Al Pacino film but here means a perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanel No 5 is a famous perfume for women, a scent made by the fashion house.

clue.text: Actor grabs at model

indicators.note: something that grabs holds another inside it, so the word at goes within the actor's name

parts.note: Shirley Temple, the child star of 1930s Hollywood

explanation.surface: A performer seizes hold of a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or model from which copies are made.

clue.text: A fair land

parts.note: fair hair is light-coloured

explanation.surface: A fair land, like a promised country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun after 'fair', but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to come down and settle, as a bird lands on a branch.

clue.text: Actor on rich food regimen

indicators.note: the answer is what sits on the word rich to make up the actor's name, so rich is taken off

parts.note: Marlene Dietrich, the German-American film star

explanation.surface: A performer goes on a diet of rich food.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Actor' as DIETRICH: the part placed 'on' RICH is what remains when RICH comes away.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a planned eating regime, here simply a regimen of food.

clue.text: Execrable starter in kebabs and processed food from cans

indicators.note: says the first letter of execrable goes inside the rearranged letters
food that is processed is broken down and reworked, so these letters are rearranged
the starter of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful starter sits among kebabs and other processed food from tins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' gives E, the first letter of Execrable, which goes 'in' the anagram of KEBABS AND ('processed').
explanation.definitionFit: Baked beans in tomato sauce are a staple tinned food, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Actor Bardot's odd characters?

wordplay.reading: the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of BARDOT, said as a list joined by and

parts.note: take the letters in odd positions of the actress's surname and say them as a list, with the word and before the last

explanation.surface: A query about Brigitte Bardot's eccentric companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of BARDOT gives B, R and O; written out with its 'and', the list spells the actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon Brando was the American screen star of On the Waterfront and The Godfather.

clue.text: Snoop or pry and sneak off

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to a snooper: pry or sneak away.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody who pokes into others' affairs is a snoop, the same meddler as the British colloquial term.

clue.text: Like a simple tune? Wrong actor

parts.note: a sin is a wrong, a moral offence
Clark Gable, star of Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: An actor gets a simple tune wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple tune is easy to carry with the voice, so it can be sung readily.

clue.text: How solid is refuse around squat?

indicators.note: says the word for refuse goes round the word for squat

parts.note: to deny is to refuse
to squat is to sit, crouching low

explanation.surface: A question whether rubbish lying around a squatted building is solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like rubbish, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Density measures mass per volume, how compact or solid a material is.

clue.text: Instruction leaflet ultimately wet

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word leaflet

parts.note: weather that is wet means it is raining

explanation.surface: An instruction leaflet ends up soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Training is teaching or instruction in a skill.

clue.text: Actor not vacuous, sweet

parts.note: Henry, Jane or Peter Fonda, the acting family

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outer letters, so the inside of not is dropped

explanation.surface: An actor who is not empty-headed is sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugary paste used in confectionery, so a sweet.

clue.text: One inspired by high earning African

indicators.note: taken in like breath, so the letter for one goes inside
someone high is out of their head, so the letters of earning are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An African high earner is a source of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' scrambles EARNING, and I ('One') goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nigerian is a native of Nigeria, a West African country.

clue.text: Knock top prize money

indicators.note: used as a verb, to top is to cut off the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: winnings are money gained from a prize or bet

explanation.surface: A burglar's knock at the door, or knocking the top prize money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' removes W from WINNINGS. In cricket a batsman's knock is a spell of batting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket slang a knock is a batsman's stay at the crease, his turn to bat.

clue.text: Actor punched by a clergyman

indicators.note: the actor's name is struck through by the letter a, which goes inside it

parts.note: Charlie Chaplin, the silent film comedian

explanation.surface: A performer is hit by a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a priest attached to a chapel, regiment or institution.

clue.text: Antique possessed by female actor

indicators.note: the word for antique is held inside the word for female

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
antique means old

explanation.surface: An old item belongs to an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: William Holden was the American star of Sunset Boulevard and Stalag 17.

clue.text: Actor after small slipper for Father Christmas?

indicators.note: says the actor's name follows the letter for small

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Vivien Leigh, Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: An actor chasing a small slipper to play Father Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipper' looks like footwear; here it is something that slips over snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's vehicle glides across the snow on runners, so it slips along.

clue.text: Deep wound reported as plank sat upon

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: the deep is the sea, and a wound is a sore; said in a British accent they match the plank's name

explanation.surface: A deep wound described as a plank someone sat on.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground teeter-totter is a balanced plank that children sit on at each end.

clue.text: Wonderful outstanding actor beginning in theatre, Italian

indicators.note: read as out-standing, the word for wonderful stands outside the rest

parts.note: fine means excellent or wonderful
Sophia Loren, the Italian film star

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wonderful Italian actor makes a start in theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' is read as standing outside: the word for wonderful wraps the actor plus the T from 'beginning in theatre'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Florentine is a native of Florence, the Tuscan city, so an Italian.

clue.text: See 2
Musical — characters associated, primarily, with Eliot

indicators.note: takes the first letters of the two words before it

parts.note: T. S. Eliot, the poet

explanation.surface: A musical whose characters are associated chiefly with Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: the show sets Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lloyd Webber show is one of the longest-running stage musicals.

clue.text: Put down setter, entertained by actor

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so the setter goes inside

parts.note: James Dean, star of Rebel Without a Cause
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A setter is put down while being entertained by an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone down is to belittle or humiliate them, lowering their dignity.

clue.text: Lincolnshire town actor, overactor?

parts.note: Cary Grant or Hugh Grant
a ham is an actor who overacts

explanation.surface: A town in Lincolnshire with an actor who overacts.
explanation.walkthrough: Grantham is a market town in Lincolnshire, an English county; it was Margaret Thatcher's birthplace.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a market town in Lincolnshire, an eastern English county, birthplace of Margaret Thatcher.
